summary.en: Ethiopian-linked drones have struck homes and a United Nations building in Khartoum, killing four, while Sudanese forces intercepted additional drones aimed at the capital. Simultaneously, clashes on Ethiopia's southern border with Kenya at Moyale have disrupted livelihoods and displaced people, prompting travel warnings and calls for refugee support. In the Amhara region, the Fano insurgency continues to threaten water security in the Nile Basin, adding a new dimension to the Horn of Africa conflict. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
